body:
Sofia Ivanova: quick review thread for the two-queue scheduler PR. main questions: fairness window + queue draining behavior. link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/8433

GitHub: PR #8433 opened by Marcus Reed: "Implement two-queue dispatch policy (short-first with fairness window) in runtime scheduler".

Marcus Reed: context: current impl is strict short-first until either (a) short queue empty or (b) fairness window expires (time-based, default 40ms). then we service 1 from long queue and reset window.

Lena Fischer: I like the shape, but I’m worried about “drain short until window hits” when short arrival is bursty. you can end up with long queue never getting picked if short keeps arriving just under the window. fairness becomes “best effort”.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. we saw something like this in the local replay: long queue wait p99 goes unbounded under sustained short trickle. window resets too eagerly.

Marcus Reed: hmm the reset is currently on *dispatch*, not on *completion*. so even if short keeps arriving, the clock keeps running. but if we’re dispatching short prefill batches quickly, we might be constantly “within the window”.

Julian Moore: reading code: `fair_until = now + window` is set when we last served long. but on each short dispatch we don’t decrement anything besides time. so if short prefill is fast, we’ll dispatch a ton of short before time elapses.

Sofia Ivanova: that’s the intended latency benefit, but we need a guard that long doesn’t starve when short is “fast” but continuous.

Jonas Weber: perf note: time-based windows are tricky because they’re coupled to GPU speed / kernel selection. on H100 vs A10 you’ll get different fairness behavior. can we do token-based / work-based budget instead?

Marcus Reed: I can switch to “serve long every N short dispatches” (dispatch-count fairness) or “after X short prefill tokens” (estimated). I avoided token estimates bc classifier is still stubby.

Lena Fischer: simplest robust: periodic long service w/ a max wait bound. like: if oldest long has waited > T_max, force-pick long next. (even if short present)

Omar El-Sayed: that pairs well w/ the starvation metrics we wanted anyway. T_max could start conservative (e.g., 500ms?) and tighten later.

Hiro Tanaka: question: what does “service 1 from long queue” mean exactly? 1 request prefill can be huge and can block decode batches. if the long request is a massive prefill, it can monopolize the step.

Marcus Reed: in PR it’s “dispatch next request from long queue into the batch builder”, not “run entire long prefill standalone”. we still do continuous batching, but yes, a giant prefill can dominate compute for the step.

Grace Kim: that’s the other concern: draining behavior inside a batch. if batch builder greedily packs prefills, you can still priority invert even if dispatch chooses “short” first. we saw a bug like that earlier.

Julian Moore: +1. in the current code path, once we decide long vs short, we still fill remaining slots from whichever queue is non-empty. so if long picked first and it has depth, it will fill the batch and short waits for next iteration.

Sofia Ivanova: can we make “draining” bounded? e.g., pick a primary queue, but only take up to K requests or up to prefill_tokens_budget from it, then allow the other queue to contribute.

Marcus Reed: yep. easiest is cap by count: when policy selects long, only take 1 (or up to `long_fill_max`) from long per batch build, then fill rest from short if any. symmetric optional.

Lena Fischer: that seems important. otherwise your fairness window doesn’t matter if a single long selection causes batch domination.

Omar El-Sayed: also note: streaming interactive requests are mostly decode-heavy after first token. for them, “short queue” should probably bias toward decode steps, not just prompt length. but for this PR, bounding long fill per *batch build* probably gets us 80%.

Jonas Weber: can we get an A/B microbench in the PR description? something like: mixed 90% short/10% long, long prompt=8k, short=256. measure short p95 latency and long wait p99 with/without fill cap.

Marcus Reed: I can add a microbench case. there’s already `scheduler_microbench_mixed.toml` in the branch. will paste numbers once CI runs.

Hiro Tanaka: also watch kernel selection confounder: if the mix changes sequence lengths per step, you might flip attention kernels. make sure the bench logs kernel choice or pins it.

Omar El-Sayed: we can log `attn_kernel_id` in the benchmark output (we already capture it in perf runs). for this PR, maybe just note “kernel stable” based on traces.

Sofia Ivanova: action items I’m hearing:
1) replace pure time-window fairness with either max-wait override or work-based budget (prefer max-wait override for prototype)
2) add cap on draining per batch build when long is selected (prevent batch domination)
3) add microbench + note kernel stability

Marcus Reed: sounds good. I’ll push an update tonight. might split into follow-up PR for clarity, but I think it’s small enough to keep in #8433.

Julian Moore: pls also add a metric so we can debug in prod: `scheduler_forced_long_dispatch_total` (counter) and maybe `long_oldest_wait_ms` (gauge or sampled log). helps validate max-wait.

Omar El-Sayed: and a trace annotation when max-wait triggers, so we can see if it’s thrashing.

Sofia Ivanova: ok. keep it behind the feature flag. once updated, tag me + Lena for re-review.

Marcus Reed: will do. :thumbsup:
